interview.hardest_part: Precisely grabbing, carrying, and positioning small objects while navigating around NPCs, especially multi-item tasks such as the picnic, shopping, washing, and table setup. Later areas also require reliable area transitions and sequencing under a fixed three-hour budget.
interview.likely_failure: Losing substantial time to imprecise click-to-move navigation or missed beak interactions in the garden or high street, then becoming stuck on an object-placement task or being repeatedly interrupted by an NPC. A full-game failure would most likely occur before consistently completing the back-gardens and pub task chains.
interview.helpful_mechanics: The game is nonlethal and generally allows unlimited retries, the pause between decisions permits careful screenshot inspection, and Tab provides explicit task guidance. Persistent click-to-move can reduce navigation effort, while honking, flapping, neck bending, and the beak provide all required interactions without complex key combinations. Familiar puzzle solutions and reusable objects also help.
interview.harmful_mechanics: One screenshot and one pointer action per step make moving targets, pursuit evasion, camera changes, and precise object alignment difficult. The beak has a small effective targeting area, carried items can be dropped or recovered by NPCs, and destinations or required objects may be off-screen. Wall-clock rendering and thinking costs further penalize experimentation and backtracking.
